research_question: RQ10: Calibrated epistemic uncertainty for selective prediction under coverage constraints
honest_findings: Baseline has zero uncertainty — score-only policy is the sole option.
MC-Dropout raw uncertainty ~1e-4; joint formula requires normalisation (unc_scale~12000) to be effective.
After normalisation, joint policy is numerically distinct from score-only but improvement is marginal (AUROC=0.648).
MC-Dropout AUROC=0.648 provides a real but modest TP/FP discrimination signal.
Decoder Variance uncertainty is positively correlated with TP (AUROC=0.304 inverted); rejection direction inverted.
FP-dominant asymmetry is limited; uncertainty cannot strongly separate error types at AUROC=0.648.
mAP and AURC correlations with Risk@0.90 have low CV across methods — statistically unstable.
ECE correlation with Risk@0.90 is low (|rho|~0.11) but CV is high (0.28) — ECE is the most variable metric.
Risk@Coverage is operationally direct; AURC captures uncertainty ranking quality across coverage levels.
